High-level proposal for discussion:
1) Offer an "uprate amendment" for the 9-month window where new baseline = current commit * 1.30; bill pro-rata for the remainder of the current invoice period.
2) Apply a blended discount: keep their current discount on existing volume, and offer a modest uplift discount (we can propose 5% on incremental usage above baseline while the amendment is active). On conversion to co-term and annualized commit, re-evaluate within renewal playbook (we can fold uplift into a single annualized commit with tiered pricing).
3) If they want immediate cost predictability, offer an annualize option: they pre-commit the 30% uplift for the remainder of the year at a 7% uplift discount (higher than the temporary 5%), with co-term normalization to 2028-12-31.

Risk/ops notes: autoscaling/priority needs to be documented — Monica, if there are additional SLAs or dedicated capacity implications, flag now.

I can draft numbers using their current monthly baseline (I have that in the HubSpot record). I'll attach a worksheet with the two price paths (temporary top-up vs annualized pre-commit) and expected invoice impact.

Subject: Connector Health — proposed amendment & pricing options

Elliot —

Thanks for the details and congrats on the pilot win. Below are two commercially viable paths; I summarized the impact and attached the draft amendment + worksheet for your review.

Option A — Temporary top-up (recommended for flexibility):
- 30% uplift on current committed baseline, effective start: 2027-05-01 for 9 months (ends 2028-01-01).
- Billing: pro-rata for remaining days in current invoice period, then monthly.
- Pricing: incremental volume receives a 5% uplift discount (incremental only). Existing baseline pricing and discounts remain unchanged.
- Pros: low up-front spend, easy to unwind at end of term.
- Cons: slightly higher unit cost for incremental traffic.

Option B — Annualize + co-term (recommended for predictability):
- Convert the 30% uplift into a pre-committed annual uplift, co-term to 2028-12-31.
- Billing: annualized commit with monthly invoicing, pro-rated only at sign.
- Pricing: blended discount applied across total annualized commit; proposed uplift discount 7% for the incremental volume when folded into the annual commit.
- Pros: lower unit economics, stable provisioning, priority for capacity.
- Cons: requires a firm annual commitment and an amendment to co-term contracts.

Next steps:
1) If you prefer Option A, we can send a 1-page amendment to sign (attached RWD-Amendment-v2.pdf) and start the uplift on 2027-05-01.
2) If you prefer Option B, we'll prepare a DocuSign amendment to annualize and co-term; I included our proposed numbers in Commit-Worksheet.xlsx.
3) Open to a hybrid: start with Option A for 3 months, then convert to Option B if the ramp meets targets — we can include a conversion checkbox in the amendment.

I've cc'd Rishi for the commercial numbers and Monica for operational confirmation. If convenient, let's schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the math.

Best —
